六级大纲词汇 · 06英文原文

The Streak That Followed the Camera

跟着相机移动的光痕 · 589 词 · 7 段 · 首次出现的目标词加粗

1At a school observatory, Nia photographed a comet. A second luminous streak appeared by its tail. The club drafted an excited caption. Nia saw a faint galaxy through binoculars, but could discern only one tail. Her teacher used zoom to show how optical distortion could magnify a scratch on an optic. She varied one parameter in the optical system. When she turned the camera, the star field moved. The streak stayed fixed.

2A friend proposed a second hypothesis. A corridor lamp might illuminate a seam in the opaque cover. Nia used a torch of analogous brightness as an analogue for the lamp. Its light did permeate the cover and radiate from a metal tube. She sealed the seam. The radiant glow vanished, but the line remained. A dark exposure with no illumination reaching the lens showed the same discrepancy. One plausible explanation had failed.

3Nia compared the line with an actual spectrum. In class, mercury and nitrogen lamps had given lines linked to each gas's molecular structure. A molecule, a metal oxide, and sulfur vapor could give distinct patterns. They had also discussed radioactivity. Uranium could emit radiation without glowing. A bright mark alone could not identify a radioactive source. In every dark frame the same strip reached the same numerical value to two decimal places. A random source rarely made so symmetric a pattern. The cause seemed intrinsic to the camera.

4To explain why a similar appearance did not establish a source, her teacher made an analogy with two dyes. He showed how to distill water, then added some to a plant extract. Its color began to diffuse. A time-lapse video made the diffusion visible. To dilute a color was to reduce its saturation. After dilution the liquid was homogeneous. A chemist could synthesize a similar shade in the lab. The synthetic dye came from a different synthesis. Nia wondered if the line would still appear if they changed the instrument rather than the view.

5First Nia plotted the correlation between exposure time and brightness. The readings began to correlate until the pixels started to saturate. An equation with an exponent above one fitted the first readings poorly. A steady extra current gave a better fit. A faulty transistor might supply it and explain the deviation at high exposure. Their deductive test rested on one premise. If that was the underlying fault, the line would follow the camera. It did when two groups exchanged cameras. A technician's rigorous test gave them empirical evidence that the faulty component did underlie the error.

6Nia used the equation to remove the signal. To differentiate a subtle speck from the original line, she tried an inversion. She could invert an earlier blank image and find the same speck there. At the optimal exposure its effect was negligible. The class checked the procedure against a pendulum they filmed to demonstrate inertia. From changes in its position they could estimate velocity by differentiation. The extra speck stayed put even when the pendulum moved. The two events could coincide without one causing the other. Their earlier intuition had confused coincidence with cause.

7A visitor asked which picture showed the discovery. Nia asked a hypothetical question. "What would a genuine comet look like with the lid on?" He pointed to the dark frame. The answer was deducible from it alone. The teacher called it an ingenious test and praised its rigor. Its ingenuity lay in using pictures a visitor could check in the right order. What began in perplexity ended in a conclusion he could test.

六级大纲词汇 · 06中文译文

跟着相机移动的光痕

按英文段落顺序对照阅读

1在学校天文台，妮娅拍下了一颗彗星。彗尾旁边又出现了一道发亮的条纹，社团兴奋地拟好了照片说明。妮娅用双筒望远镜望见一个暗淡的星系，却只辨认出一条尾巴。老师用变焦功能示范光学畸变如何放大光学元件上的划痕。妮娅在光学系统里只改了一个参数。她转动相机，星野跟着转，条纹却留在原处。

2一位同学提出第二个假设，走廊里的灯光可能照进不透明外罩的接缝。妮娅用一支亮度接近的手电筒模拟走廊灯。光确实透过外罩，又从金属筒上反射出来。她封住接缝，亮光消失了，条纹仍在。挡住镜头拍一张暗场照片，那个异常也依旧存在。一个看似合理的解释被排除了。

3妮娅把条纹和实际光谱作比较。课堂上，汞灯和氮灯的谱线都与各自的分子结构有关。分子、金属氧化物和硫蒸气可以形成不同的光谱。他们也谈过放射性，铀可以释放辐射而不发出可见光。仅凭一个亮斑，无法认定有放射源。每张暗场照片上，同一排像素的数值精确到小数点后两位都一致。随机信号很少形成这么对称的图案。原因似乎出在相机内部。

4老师用两种染料打比方，说明外观相似不足以判定来源。他先示范怎样蒸馏水，再把一些蒸馏水加到植物提取液里。颜色逐渐扩散，延时视频把这个过程显示出来。颜色稀释后，饱和度下降，液体变得均匀。化学家也可以在实验室合成相似的颜色，可合成染料有不同的生成过程。这个比较让妮娅有了明确的检验办法，保持拍摄对象不变，只换相机，看那道线是否还会出现。

5妮娅先画出曝光时间与亮度的关系。像素尚未饱和时，读数随曝光时间变化。指数大于一的方程对最初几组读数拟合得不好。假设有一股稳定的额外电流，结果就更吻合。故障晶体管可能漏出这股电流，也能解释长时间曝光时出现的偏差。小组据此作了一个推理，如果问题出在相机里，条纹应该跟着相机走。两个小组交换相机后，果然如此。技术人员通过严谨的测试证实，出故障的元件确实造成了异常。

6妮娅用方程扣除异常信号。为了区分一粒很淡的斑点和原来那道线，她把图像反相，在之前的空白照片里也找到了同一个点。在最合适的曝光时间下，它的影响微乎其微。全班又用演示惯性时拍下的摆锤检验处理方法。对摆锤的位置变化做微分，可以估算速度。摆锤一直在动，多出的斑点却待在原地。两个现象可以同时出现，彼此未必有因果关系。他们原先凭直觉把巧合当成了原因。

7一位访客问，哪张照片拍到了他们的发现。妮娅问了一个假设性的问题，盖上镜头盖时，真正的彗星应该是什么样？访客指了指暗场照片，光看这一张就能推出答案。老师称赞这个测试巧妙又严谨。巧妙之处在于，访客可以按顺序亲自核对几张照片。原先让人困惑的现象，最后成了一个他自己就能检验的结论。
